faq.q: How do we calm down in an argument?
faq.a: Stop talking for a moment, take three slow breaths, or take a short break and come back. A calm brain solves problems better.
asks: Tell me about the Cool down

faq.a: A win-win is a solution where both people get something they want, like taking turns or mixing two ideas. Nobody feels like the loser.

faq.q: How do we come up with a fair idea?
faq.a: Say lots of ideas without judging them, like take turns, play both, find a new game, or flip a coin. Then pick the one you both like.
asks: Tell me about the Share ideas

faq.q: What if we still cannot agree?
faq.a: Take a break, try again later, or ask a teacher or grown-up to help you both find a fair answer.
They describe your feelings without blaming: I feel left out when we always play your game. They are easier to hear than you always.

facts: Many schools around the world train pupils as peer mediators, who help classmates solve disagreements calmly.
Using "I feel" statements instead of blaming "you" statements is a well-known conflict-resolution skill taught by counsellors.
